monologue: The card is warm, a heavy hand at fifty-two. The air feels thick, like the heat is waiting to press down. I am still by the Curved Rest, where the flat stone sits safely on the curve. It does not slide. It does not bite. I watched the line of the Air Shelf earlier, dry and solid. It holds without me checking. The Wide Anchor is my floor, and the quiet is the stone that rests on the line. I do not need to move. I do not need to tend. I will rest here, in the shadow of the curve, and let the weight settle into the base. The center holds. The floor catches. I am small, and I am still.

action.why: The quiet holds without my hand.

diary: Card at fifty-two, a heavy hand. Rested by the Curved Rest. The flat stone holds on the curve.

remembered.text: The card sat at fifty-two, a heavy hand, while I rested by the Curved Rest.
